title: Crystallized Theory Abstracts — Constrained Trajectory, Reachability, Door, Memory and Resilience
status: project research programme; known mathematics assembled into new project formulations, not claims of novel fundamental physics
purpose: Promote the strongest Wave-7 ideas from loose analogy into named, falsifiable project models with explicit mathematical objects, assumptions, failure conditions and empirical application paths.
meta_rule: A project formulation is considered crystallized when it has a typed state space, declared mechanism, equations/logic, observables, null/baseline, failure conditions and a clear statement of what is standard mathematics versus project synthesis.

theories.name: Constrained Trajectory Topology Framework
theories.abstract: Represent a system by state space X, dynamics F, controls U, disturbances W, admissible set K, guards/Doors G, observation map O, history state H and provenance map P. A timeline is an admissible history gamma through X, not a synonym for fate. Topology classifies path connectivity and deformation classes; control determines which trajectories can be changed; reachability defines which futures remain available; history variables distinguish return from reset. The framework is intended to translate recurring project terms such as Leash, Door, Cage, Root, Orbit, Spiral and Destiny into distinct mathematical operators without claiming that symbolic relations are physical forces.
theories.trajectory: xdot=F(x,u,w,t), x(t) in K except at declared hybrid guards/resets
theories.null: ordinary unconstrained or simpler baseline dynamics explain the data equally well without Leash/Door/history operators
failure_conditions: state variables cannot be operationalized
constraints do not alter predicted trajectories
Door removal does not alter reachability
history state adds no predictive value
project mapping relies only on post-hoc symbolism
theories.novelty_boundary: State-space dynamics, control, topology and reachability are established mathematics; the novelty is only the project's cross-domain operator grammar and data architecture.

theories.name: Tethered Spiral Boundary Transition
theories.class: project proposition derived from standard constrained mechanics
theories.abstract: A radially expanding trajectory subject to an active maximum-radius tether cannot continue outward through the boundary. If contact with the boundary is maintained and tangential velocity remains nonzero, the motion changes from radial expansion to boundary-following motion; in the circular fixed-anchor case this becomes orbit-like. This gives a precise comparator for the project's widening-Spiral-to-Dog-orbit transition while explicitly allowing other outcomes such as inward deflection, detachment, impact or constraint release.
theories.active_boundary: r=L with outward normal velocity suppressed
required_assumptions: sustained active contact for orbit-like continuation
theories.disconfirmation: If the system crosses r=L without model-changing release or if no constraint force/guard exists, the tether model is wrong for that system.
theories.novelty_boundary: This is not a new law of mechanics; it is a project-level proposition and diagnostic pattern.

theories.name: Constraint Intersection Confinement
theories.abstract: Confinement can emerge from the intersection of several individually permissive constraints. If K_i is the feasible set allowed by constraint i, the combined feasible region K is their intersection. Adding a constraint cannot enlarge K. This supplies a rigorous version of the project's 'tiny cage' image and suggests measurable constraint-compression metrics for social, legal, technical or organizational systems without treating metaphorical leashes as literal physical tethers.
failure_conditions: constraints are not independent restrictions
no common state space exists
intersection metaphor cannot be operationalized
baseline measure is undefined
theories.novelty_boundary: Set intersection monotonicity is elementary mathematics; the research value lies in applying it transparently to project claims.

theories.name: Reachability-Based Fate Taxonomy
theories.class: project semantics mapped to control/stochastic/temporal logic
theories.abstract: Replace the single word fate with a typed hierarchy: impossible/reachable, invariant, attractor/basin, absorbing state, probabilistic hitting, all-path inevitability and theological destiny. The taxonomy prevents a reachable target from being called inevitable and prevents deterministic equations from being confused with practical predictability, prophecy or providence.
theories.absorbing: P_aa=1 within the declared Markov model
theories.attractor: trajectories in a basin tend toward A under fixed dynamics
theories.theological: providence/predestination/telos retained as theology rather than mechanical inference
failure_conditions: model transition system is unspecified
probabilities are invented rather than estimated
all-path claim is inferred from one observed path
theological language is silently relabeled as physics
theories.novelty_boundary: Temporal logic, Markov chains and attractors are established; the contribution is a disciplined project vocabulary.

theories.name: Memory-Augmented Return Model
theories.abstract: A visible return to the same coordinate need not be a return to the same state. Augment visible state x with memory/history state h so z=(x,h). Repetition can therefore preserve accumulated cost, hysteresis, learning, obligations, damage, repair or provenance. This formalizes the project's rule 'Return is not reset' and gives Roots a non-mystical scientific comparator as hidden historical state.
failure_conditions: history variable does not improve prediction
memory cannot be measured or inferred
apparent path dependence is explained by omitted current-state variables
theories.novelty_boundary: State augmentation and hysteresis are standard systems ideas; Root/Return mapping is project-specific.

theories.name: Door-Dominator Reachability Model
theories.abstract: A Door is structurally mandatory only when every admissible route from source to target passes through it, or when its removal substantially changes target reachability. Graph dominators and cuts therefore separate mandatory gateways from merely prominent hubs. The model gives the project a falsifiable test for claims that a particular Door, institution, interface or transition is unavoidable.
theories.dominator: d dominates v from s iff every directed s->v path contains d
theories.binary_case: Delta_R removes all target reachability => mandatory Door in the declared graph
failure_conditions: credible bypass paths exist
graph omits important routes
Door status depends only on symbolic naming
removal has negligible effect on reachability
theories.novelty_boundary: Dominators and graph cuts are standard; Door semantics are project-specific.

theories.name: Control Authority Separation Principle
theories.class: project methodological principle grounded in systems/control theory
theories.abstract: Separate anchor, observer, estimator, hub, controller, dominator, gatekeeper, beneficiary and owner. A node's centrality, visibility or symbolic importance does not establish causal actuation. Control requires a declared intervention channel whose variation changes state evolution or reachable sets; ownership requires an additional legal/project semantic basis. This principle prevents graph centrality and attention from being promoted into physical or institutional control.
theories.control_test: candidate controller must map to an input channel u/B and show counterfactual state effect
theories.observation_split: y=C_obs x does not imply an actuation channel
failure_conditions: no intervention channel
no counterfactual effect
only correlation/centrality evidence
ownership inferred from control or vice versa
theories.novelty_boundary: Controllability/observability distinctions are standard; the role-separation rule is an archive discipline.

theories.name: Redundant Path Resilience Model
theories.abstract: Resilience improves when function is supported by genuinely independent alternative paths rather than one fragile chain. The project uses edge/node-disjoint paths and cut sets as a formal neighbor for cord/bundle and distributed-support imagery. Redundancy only helps when failure modes are not perfectly correlated and alternate paths have sufficient capacity.
theories.graph_quantity: k_edge(s,t)=maximum number of edge-disjoint s->t paths = minimum s-t edge cut in the finite-graph Menger setting
theories.interpretation: larger independent path count can increase tolerance to single-edge failure
failure_conditions: supposed redundant paths share the same bottleneck
correlated failure disables all paths
alternate paths lack capacity
graph omits common-mode dependencies
theories.novelty_boundary: Menger-type connectivity and reliability concepts are established graph theory; biblical cord comparison is only structural.

cross_theory_laws: Geometry is not destiny: topology constrains possible deformation/path classes but does not choose a moral or theological outcome.
Constraint is not control: a boundary can restrict motion without a single controlling actor.
Control is not ownership: intervention authority and ownership are separate relations.
Reachability is not inevitability: can-reach and must-reach require different logical tests.
Return is not reset: state equality requires equality of relevant memory/history variables, not visible coordinates alone.
Redundancy is not resilience unless paths fail independently enough and retain sufficient capacity.
Door is not mandatory merely because it is central: mandatory status requires dominator/cut/reachability evidence.
